feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it makes no claim about its result. Evidence: iteration 4 (16 mm, y=0.05, wheel_track 0.08, mass 0.8, body 0.18, score 58.54) is the best measured design. Iteration 8 (y=0.03) fell to 41.1, so the sensor lead should stay at y=0.05. Iteration 9 (12 mm footprint, 58.27) was neutral, so footprint is not a strong lever. Iterations 5 and 6 (wheel_radius 0.04 at 41.4, and mass 1.0 at 42.7) cut s-bend progress sharply, which suggests added speed or inertia can overshoot. Iteration 2 (lighter, shorter body with y=0.07) also scored lower. I kept the iteration 4 controller so that body_length is the only variable. When the next race reports: if s-bend or slalom max_error and steering_oscillation fall while progress holds at or above 0.185, keep body_length 0.24 m and do not add more inertia. If progress falls below about 0.18 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, return body_length to 0.18 m, since inertia is overshooting. If the score is flat, body_length is inert and the next geometry test is a wider sensor span.
requested_changes: If the score holds or rises with max_error and steering_oscillation falling on the s-bend and slalom: keep body_length at 0.24 m and do not raise mass further. Evidence: iteration 6 (mass 1.0, about 25 percent more inertia) cut s-bend progress from 0.185 to 0.065, so more inertia is not automatically better.

If progress falls below about 0.18 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2: return body_length to 0.18 m and keep sensor_size 0.016 m. Evidence: iteration 2 (lighter body plus y=0.07) lost s-bend progress, and iteration 6 showed extra inertia also cuts progress, so the best measured inertia sits near the iteration 4 value.

If body_length is inert (score within about 1 point of 58.5): test the sensor span at x = -0.07 to 0.07 m with 16 mm footprints and body_length 0.18 m. Evidence: iterations 1 to 4 showed that widening the span cut line loss, and line loss is still about 0.85 to 0.95 per run on the slalom and s-bend.
